GENERAL REQUIREMENTS AND CLASSIFICATION OF TESTS FOR MICRO CIRCUITS
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 24 April 1981, after the draft finalized by the Semiconductor Devices and Integrated Circuits Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. 0.2 This standard deals with general requirements, such as material, construction and workmanship, marking, procedure for approval of devices ( type approval and batch acceptance ) including classification of tests, etc, as applied to monolithic, multichip and hybrid micro circuits. This standard is a necessary adjunct to relevant Indian Standard which may include, among other things, details of ratings, characteristic values, dimensions and other applicable requirements. 0.3 While preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from the following documents: BS 9400 : 1970 Specification for integrated electronic circuits of assessed quality: Generic data and methods of test. British Standards Institution. JSS 51400 ( Part I )-1972 General requirements for micro circuits. Directorate of Standardization, Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, New Delhi. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This Indian Standard relates to the general requirements, classiiication of tests and other related aspects as applicable to micro circuits ( monolithic, multichip and hybrid ). 2. TERMINOLOGY, SYMBOLS GRAPHICAL SYMBOLS AND LETTER

CONSTRUCTION

AND

WORKMANSHIP

4.1 Material - The devices shall be constructed from materials free from flaws and other defects. The material used for construction shall not be susceptible to any mutual chemical reaction, shall be non-flammable, non-explosive and non-corrosive.
4.2 Construction-The methods of attachment ( for example soldering, welding wrapping ) of the terminations shall be proper and such that all the electrical connections are mechanically secure and electrically continuous. 4.3 Workmanship - All the components shall be manufactured processed in a thoroughly workman-like manner and in accordance good design and sound engineering practice. and with

4.4 Finish - Unless otherwise specified all exposed materials liable. to the deterioration in moist or corrosive atmosphere shall be given suitable finish. 5. GENERAL

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. 7.3 Test Incidence - Group 0 tests shall be carried out prior to the commencement of tests on subsequent groups and the results shall be recorded. Each test shall be applied in the order listed and where measurements are required the results shall be recorded. Where tests are not applicable, they shall be indicated in the relevant detail specification. 8. BATCH ACCEPTANCE PROCEDURE

8.1 Lot or Batch - Unless otherwise specified in the relevant detail specification, a lot or batch shall be as specified in IS : 2612-1965" and shall consist of micro circuits of a single type or may consist of a collection of sub-batches of electrically and structurally similar devices produced under essentially same conditions and offered for inspection at one time. Where a batch identification is terminated upon completion of wafer or substrate processing, or at any later point prior to device sealing, it shall be possible to process more than a single device type in a production batch provided all device types are structurally similar. 8.1.1 In the case of structurally similar devices, grouping of specimens for acceptance tests during batch acceptance shall be similar to that specified for type approval tests in the relevant detail specification. 8.2 Acceptance Tests --Tests bracketed together subgroup are considered as sequence and should be using the same specimen. within a group or performed as such

8.2.1 Group A Tests-Group A tests shall be performed as given in Table 2 and shall consist of visual examination and electrical parameters Group A test may be specified in the relevant detail specification. performed in any order. 8.2.2 Group B Tests - These tests shall be performed Table 3. This inspection shall be applied to specimens satisfied the specified Group A test requirements. 8.2.3 Failures - Failure of a device will be counted as a single failure. as given in which have

in one or more tests of a subgroup

8.2.4 Resubmitted Batch -- Batches which have been tested and from which defectives have been screened out and which are resubmitted by batch acceptance procedure once again shall contain devices which were in the original batch. Resubmitted lots shall be kept separate from new lots and shall be clearly identified as resubmitted lots. No batch may be *Recommendation components. for type approval and sampling procedures for electronic

8

IS : 9596 - 1981 resubmitted for Group A tests after a second rejection for the same defect. No batch may be resubmitted for Group I3 tests after a second rejection. At the discretion of the testing authority, testing of characteristics which are not affected by the screening process may be omitted for resubmitted batches. In all instances where analysis of the failed devices indicates that the failure mechanism is due to basic processing procedure, a basic design fault or nonscreenable defects, the lot shall not be resubmitted.

8.2.4.1 Group B tests for the resubmitted batches shall be applied to specimens that have satisfied the specified Group A test requirements. 8.2.4.2 Resubmitted batches shall be tested for all characteristics, using tightened inspection only for these characteristics in which the devices have failed. 9.
